name: employee-skill-progression-visual
description: Visual verification of employee skill progression: XP gain from a dispatched task tracked across tick checkpoints, task duration scaling by proficiency, the pending-action ghost preview persisting while its target employee is busy, the ghost disappearing once claimed, and the employee detail panel reflecting each change.

expect.note: dusty_hollow's own starting cash is $50,000 -- coincidentally the same figure the sandbox default uses, so this checks the level's own value, not a carried-over one.

steps.description: Employee A (#1) — will be dispatched to real blasting work below.
Employee B (#2) — holds a different skill (driving.truck), so the second dispatch later has nobody else on the roster able to claim it, which is what keeps its ghost preview alive.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.

expect.note: already level 1 from hiring's Rookie starting qualification -- this call is a same-level no-op, not the first level-up

steps.description: Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.

Left unmarked: no UI control drives `employee dispatch` and none should exist -- employees.ts's own case comment: "no console command currently creates one... left the Bunkhouse shift-cycle unreachable from any player-facing flow" -- a test hook by design.
tickEmployees claims the dispatch: employee A becomes busy and taskTicksRemaining is seeded from BASE_TASK_DURATION_TICKS scaled by proficiency/need/living-quarters multipliers.

Left unmarked: no UI control drives `employee dispatch` and none should exist -- employees.ts's own case comment: "no console command currently creates one... left the Bunkhouse shift-cycle unreachable from any player-facing flow" -- a test hook by design.

expect.note: the second dispatch's ghost preview -- employee A is still busy with the first task and employee B can't claim it (wrong skill), so this stays queued through the next several checkpoints

steps.description: Checkpoint 0 — task in progress, ghost preview live at the second dispatch's target tile.
Checkpoint 1 (+10 ticks) — employee A's XP bar should show partial fill from the first task's per-tick XP gain; the ghost preview for the still-unclaimed second dispatch should still be visible.

Checkpoint 2 (+60 ticks, 71 cumulative) — long enough for the first task to complete at any proficiency level and for employee A to auto-claim the second dispatch once freed, which should make its ghost preview disappear.

expect.note: the second dispatch's ghost preview disappears here -- employee A finished the first task and auto-claimed it

steps.description: Checkpoint 3 (+150 ticks, target 221 cumulative) — with real-time auto-tick no longer racing this scripted sequence (#406), tick advance is deterministic for seed:42 and a random event (politics_ev_mandate) reliably fires and auto-pauses at cumulative tick 125, 54 ticks into this step — the same event the game would show a player, not a bug this scenario should paper over. The next step resolves it so the remaining ticks below can still reach the intended final state.

Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.

expect.note: seed:42's politics_ev_mandate always fires here (per this file's own checkpoint-3 description) -- option 0 costs $60,000, genuinely applied since Finding #29's fix

steps.description: Remaining ticks to reach the checkpoint 3 target of 221 cumulative (125 + 96 = 221) now that the event no longer blocks them.

expect.note: no scalar exists for a single employee's XP/level within SerializableGameState -- only the roster-wide sum, which never crosses a level threshold across this file's 221-tick budget even though employee A genuinely works the whole time (confirmed via direct trace); the XP-bar-fill claim this file is named for is a screenshot-only assertion, not one this field can make
